subject: Maths
central_question: How can ruler-and-compass properties be used to plan and construct accurate figures?
in_scope_units: 8.1 Artwork — compass curves, circles, centre, radius, and repeated arcs
8.2 Squares and Rectangles — properties, naming, and rotated figures
8.3 Constructing Squares and Rectangles — perpendicular lines and given side lengths
8.4 Exploring Rectangles — moving points, subdivisions, centres, holes, and curves
8.5 Exploring Diagonals of Rectangles and Squares — diagonal and angle investigations
8.6 Points Equidistant from Two Given Points — circle intersections and the house construction

known_pitfalls.claim: A rotated square is no longer a square.
known_pitfalls.correction: Rotation preserves all side lengths and angles.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any order of corner labels names a rectangle.
known_pitfalls.correction: The order must follow consecutive corners around the boundary.

known_pitfalls.claim: A fixed-distance point must be found by ruler trial and error.
known_pitfalls.correction: A circle or arc locates all points at that distance.

recommended_example_progression: Construct a 4 cm radius circle and the 8 cm Wavy Wave.
Verify square and rectangle properties after rotation.
Construct a 6 cm square and given-side rectangles.
Use equal-radius arcs to construct the house.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the Construct, Figure it Out, Explore, Think, and Try tasks through Sections 8.1–8.6.
